opportunity_name: Bonded e-commerce fulfilment and returns
investor_capital_decision: 3PL or marketplace investor builds bonded fulfilment/returns near Khorgos or Almaty for Chinese sellers.
buyer_market: Chinese sellers and marketplaces serving Kazakhstan; Uzbek/Kyrgyz reach must be tested separately.
why_now: FACT [S01]: customs authorities describe 2026 e-commerce-rule changes; existing fulfilment competition is real [S02].
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing marketplace/CDEK networks and direct China parcel supply; Uzbekistan hub is a candidate, not an established strongest location.
deciding_location_factor: All-in delivered cost and delivery/returns time after destination-specific customs and last mile.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: prepositioned border/Almaty inventory can shorten service; bonded status alone does not create duty-free Uzbek access.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: eligible seller volumes and profitable throughput; national parcel growth is not contracted hub demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: bonded entitlement, destination procedures, customs guarantee and last-mile routes at an actual site.
captured_status: FACT [S02]: incumbent local services exist; Chinese-seller bonded inventory gap is not established or disproven.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: storage/pick/pack/returns fees plus faster stock turns, if savings exceed inventory, border and delivery costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Does any Chinese seller have an unserved, legally workable bonded inventory requirement?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S01 separates foreign-marketplace imports from goods already in EAEU circulation. S02 offers Kazakhstan fulfilment; neither proves a bonded gap.
key_unknown: Merchant-specific residual throughput and legal/tax treatment by destination.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: For one seller basket, verify customs/operator eligibility and compare a Khorgos/Almaty landed-cost and lead-time quote with direct-China and incumbent fulfilment quotes; identify unallocated volumes.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A named seller has unallocated repeat volumes sufficient for the operator minimum; a lawful route and conservative quote show a cost or paid service advantage.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if the required customs model is legally unavailable or incumbent supply meets the same SLA below break-even local cost; PARK if no testable volume can be obtained.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: testable service mechanism, but regulatory changes and warehouse presence do not establish an open bonded investment slot.

opportunity_name: Dedicated generation for Ekibastuz compute
investor_capital_decision: Power developer funds dedicated generation at Ekibastuz under the proposed 70/30 structure for compute customers.
buyer_market: Creditworthy data-centre power buyers and grid/single-buyer counterparties for any residual share; none contracted here.
why_now: FACT [S03]: ministry describes an adopted 70/30 framework and an interested Ekibastuz investor.
strongest_realistic_alternative: For the power investor: expansion/contracting at an existing eligible station; for mobile compute demand: overseas powered campuses. Best matched rival not established.
deciding_location_factor: Bankable offtake and full delivered firm-power cost, including the economics of the grid share.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: Ekibastuz generation infrastructure can support compute, but national policy does not allocate an individual site connection or customer.
scale_view: FACT [S04]: ECG discusses a 100 MW first-phase campus, not an awarded power offtake or demand for every new block.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: fuel technology, site water, emissions, permits, connection, uptime and construction cost.
captured_status: S03: interested investor, technical assessment and unresolved investment details; S04: campus MoU. No full-capacity capture established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: long-term direct power sales can service generation investment if both sold shares and reliability costs are covered.
cheapest_kill_test: Does the proposed generation block qualify for 70/30 and have a bankable compute buyer?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S03 explicitly describes modernization/reconstruction/expansion of existing stations, while also discussing a new Ekibastuz plant; applicability needs project-specific confirmation.
key_unknown: Eligibility of the actual new block and a financeable offtake/payment split.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Read the operative law/implementing terms for this exact block; obtain the existing project allocation and draft buyer power terms; compare full power cost with an existing-station supply offer.
pass_condition_if_uwt: The block is eligible, incremental capacity remains investable, and creditworthy contracted sales cover generation, firming and grid-share obligations in a conservative cost case.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if evidence confirms ineligibility or a buyer power ceiling below sustainable full cost; PARK if no accessible offtake or project allocation can be identified.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: the legal-policy premise has support; its application and customer economics remain decisive UWTs.

opportunity_name: Ekibastuz AI colocation and compute services
investor_capital_decision: Colocation/AI infrastructure investor builds compute capacity in the proposed Ekibastuz campus; generation is a separate investment.
buyer_market: AI labs, hyperscalers and regional enterprise/public buyers; customer-specific workloads and contracts UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S04]: ECG/KT-Telecom signed a campus MoU in August 2026; this is investor interest, not FID.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Established overseas AI campuses, including UAE/Nordics/Malaysia candidates; customer-specific strongest rival not established.
deciding_location_factor: Lawful hardware access, reliable delivered power and network performance at a competitive revenue per usable GPU/rack.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: campus power/climate may help; no verified delivered-cost or latency advantage over the best eligible campus.
scale_view: S04 proposes 100 MW initially and up to 1 GW; nameplate plans do not prove customer utilization.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: hardware/end-user clearance, firm power, cooling water, fibre redundancy, carbon and security requirements.
captured_status: ECG MoU evidenced; remaining slots and competing developer allocations UNKNOWN. MoU is not full capture.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: rack/compute-service revenue less hardware depreciation, power, network and reliability costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Can a named customer lawfully use the intended hardware here and accept the site service specification?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S05 retains ownership/end-user controls despite AI Diffusion non-enforcement. It is not evidence of a blanket Kazakhstan GPU ban. S04 records actual site consideration.
key_unknown: Hardware eligibility plus customer willingness to pay for this powered location.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Specify GPU/ECCN, owner and end user; check current BIS/vendor eligibility and one customer specification; compare delivered compute cost, firm power and connectivity with that customer's best eligible alternative.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A lawful supply path and power/network offer meet a real buyer's workload/SLA at a competitive utilization and price case, with an available campus slot.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if required hardware is unavailable to this transaction or the buyer rejects site-critical power/network/carbon terms; PARK if no concrete customer specification is obtainable.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: neither export-control pessimism nor a campus announcement settles the investor-location decision.

opportunity_name: Grid battery-storage and balancing IPP
investor_capital_decision: Storage IPP builds and operates grid batteries for capacity/balancing contracts; no battery technology or node is fixed.
buyer_market: Grid/single buyer or renewable IPPs paying for flexibility; standalone payment contract UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S06]: Mirny wind+BESS reached FID and secured financing in April 2026.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Uzbekistan standalone BESS opportunities, evidenced by EBRD-approved Celest; within Kazakhstan, integrated BESS and other flexibility.
deciding_location_factor: Procured revenue, dispatch obligations and connection availability versus full battery lifecycle cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: grid need is plausible; a bundled renewable PPA does not establish merchant/standalone storage revenue rights.
scale_view: FACT: Mirny includes 600 MWh; Celest is 150 MW/300 MWh. Neither sizes Kazakhstan's residual standalone market.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: target node, duration, grid study, degradation, augmentation, safety and dispatch access.
captured_status: Mirny has sponsors, battery supplier and financing; its BESS is allocated. Further independent contracts not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: availability/capacity/ancillary-service payments; arbitrage alone is not assumed bankable.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a currently procurable and financeable payment route for the proposed storage asset?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S06 supports an integrated project and 25-year PPA; S07 status is Approved, not operating or loan-signed. Do not transfer either structure automatically.
key_unknown: Kazakh standalone procurement, payment counterparty and project-specific cash-flow entitlement.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Locate the operative storage participation rules or an actual tender/draft service agreement; map one node and revenue/dispatch terms; compare with Uzbekistan contract economics.
pass_condition_if_uwt: An available creditworthy contract legally pays for a specified service at a node whose technical and lifecycle costs fit the contracted revenue.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if authoritative rules exclude the asset from all required payments or offered revenue cannot cover lifecycle cost; PARK if only an uncontracted system need can be shown.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: financed integrated batteries refute a blanket infeasibility claim, but do not close the standalone-IPPs revenue gap.

opportunity_name: Wind-blade manufacture
investor_capital_decision: Blade/OEM investor builds licensed wind-blade manufacturing for Kazakhstan and reachable neighbouring projects; site not secured.
buyer_market: Wind OEMs/EPCs and developers; nominated blade orders and designs UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S08]: Shu component assembly has begun; regional project supply exists [S10]. Neither proves an unfilled blade order.
strongest_realistic_alternative: OEM-approved incumbent blade supply bundled with turbine/EPC contracts; China is a supply candidate; Uzbekistan/Turkey candidates not cost-ranked.
deciding_location_factor: OEM-approved order utilization and oversized delivered-blade cost for the actual project routes.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: Kazakh fabrication could avoid some oversized freight; no verified route or licence advantage yet.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: accessible blades/year by design and delivery date; regional GW pipeline is not a transferable order book.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: OEM licence, moulds, composite inputs, quality certification, plant utilities and oversize-road/rail clearance.
captured_status: S08 identifies nacelle/hub assembly, not proof that a domestic blade line operates. S10 illustrates project-level OEM/EPC allocation.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: licensed blade margin plus avoided freight, conditional on enough compatible orders to amortize tooling.
cheapest_kill_test: Is any named wind project's blade package unawarded and open to a Kazakh manufacturing route?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S08's achieved milestone concerns turbine component assembly; S10 names Envision/CEEC at Bash. Do not infer blade supply availability from national project plans.
key_unknown: An unallocated OEM-approved order pool and feasible delivered-blade route.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Check supplier awards for two near-term regional projects; ask their OEM for licence/design and minimum run size; obtain one oversize route/freight quotation versus current supply.
pass_condition_if_uwt: At least one real unallocated programme supports an OEM-approved compatible production run and a positive delivered-cost/service case at conservative utilization.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if evidence confirms unavailable technology, physically impossible route or all target orders tied without a residual slot; PARK if accessible orders remain below the quoted viable run.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: local freight logic remains testable; an assembly plant cannot be treated as proof of either blade capture or a blade gap.

opportunity_name: Wind-tower fabrication
investor_capital_decision: Tower fabricator builds steel tower-section capacity for regional wind projects; a Zhambyl or other site remains unselected.
buyer_market: Wind OEMs/EPCs and IPPs with unallocated tower packages; orders UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT: S09 included towers in the planned factory scope; S08 records actual component assembly in 2026.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Expansion/sourcing at the Shu SANY-linked plant and incumbent imported towers; Turkey/Uzbekistan strongest rival not established.
deciding_location_factor: Qualified plate/fabrication cost plus oversized transport and firm order utilization.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity can reduce tower freight; availability/price of qualified local plate and OEM acceptance are unproven.
scale_view: S08's 2 GW/year is whole-plant nameplate, not verified tower throughput or accessible demand.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: plate grade and source, welding/corrosion qualification, factory utilities and route envelopes.
captured_status: Existing named component investment is real; achieved tower-line status and spare capacity remain UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: fabrication margin and freight savings if actual orders absorb fixed shop and qualification cost.
cheapest_kill_test: Does commissioned/committed local tower capacity already cover target orders?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S09 lists planned towers; S08 describes nacelles/hubs and an Eni order. The mismatch prevents treating planned tower capacity as proven full capture.
key_unknown: Actual tower-line commissioning/utilization and residual multi-OEM orders.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Obtain the Shu tower-line status and product capacity; match it to awarded/unawarded regional tower orders; compare one local plate/fabrication quote with incumbent delivered towers.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A distinct compatible order book remains after existing supply and covers quoted minimum shop utilization with a delivered-cost advantage.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if confirmed target tower orders are fully covered with no distinct slot or no competitive qualified supply route exists; PARK if only intermittent subscale orders remain.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: explicit tower-scope evidence deserves a capture test, not an automatic FAIL based on a whole-plant announcement.

opportunity_name: Accredited food and feed testing laboratories for export certification
investor_capital_decision: Testing/certification investor opens destination-recognised food/feed laboratory capacity near exporters; site UNKNOWN.
buyer_market: Meat, grain and food exporters paying for required tests; sample counts and willingness to pay UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S13]: Kazakhstan is covered by FMD-free-with-vaccination zones; this does not itself certify exports or laboratories.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing Kazagrex laboratories, SGS network and other recognised domestic labs before overseas sample testing.
deciding_location_factor: Recognition for the exact test/destination and total sample turnaround/cost versus existing capacity.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local testing can avoid shipping delay; incremental advantage disappears if recognised incumbents meet exporters' SLA.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: paid sample volumes by assay/destination; export tonnage is not a laboratory revenue estimate.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: importer recognition, accreditation scope, staff, equipment and sample chain of custody at a selected site.
captured_status: FACT [S11-S12]: testing incumbents exist; recognition gaps and queue capacity not established.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring per-test fees and avoided exporter delays if recognition, utilization and turnaround are competitive.
cheapest_kill_test: Do exporters actually lack destination-recognised tests with an acceptable domestic turnaround?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S12 describes an accredited multi-city network; S11 markets food-testing services. Neither is a register proving China/EU/Gulf recognition for every assay.
key_unknown: Assay-specific recognition/capacity gap that exporters will pay to close.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Match one exporter's required assays to current destination recognition registers and two domestic lab quotes; annualise its paid sample schedule and compare with a modular lab minimum.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A documented recognition or delay gap supports a viable paid sample pool and a feasible accreditation/recognition route at a specific site.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if required recognition is unavailable or recognised incumbents satisfy the same SLA below viable cost; PARK if the remaining sample pool is too small.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: incumbency weakens the claimed gap but does not disprove a specialised recognised service opening.

opportunity_name: Integrated UKTMP-linked titanium melting and powder
investor_capital_decision: Aerospace melter/forger funds the original integrated UKTMP-linked melting-and-powder package at Ust-Kamenogorsk; do not split it.
buyer_market: Aerospace tier-1 and AM-material buyers; demand for this new integrated package UNKNOWN.
why_now: SOURCE THESIS: sponge scarcity and UKTMP expansion; exact current bottleneck and customer programme not independently established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing qualified downstream chain, including Aubert & Duval/UKAD, and Japanese sponge plus established melting/powder supply; strongest package-specific rival UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: Product/process qualification, secure usable feed and conversion yield/cost, not inherited sponge certification.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: proximity to UKTMP feed may help; qualification and utilization of both new downstream steps remain independent requirements.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: contracted tonnes by alloy/powder specification and compatible melting/atomisation utilization.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: feed rights/quality, power, vacuum/atomisation capability, inert gas, yields and new-line customer qualification.
captured_status: FACT [S14]: established downstream corporate chain exists; current UKTMP partner appetite and any open integrated slot UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: margin on qualified downstream products after conversion, yield loss and qualification cost; no sponge-to-powder premium assumed.
cheapest_kill_test: Is melting/powder actually the buyer bottleneck and can the whole proposed package be qualified and supplied?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S14 records A&D sole ownership of UKAD in 2022 and absorption in 2025. Historical partnership descriptions cannot establish a current open JV. UKTMP site fetch failed.
key_unknown: Buyer-backed need and qualification path for the integrated package, with uncommitted UKTMP feed/participation.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Check current UKTMP expansion/partner scope and one aerospace/powder buyer specification; map qualification milestones, feed commitments and incumbent conversion quotes for the intact package.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A buyer identifies unmet qualified downstream capacity, both process steps have a feasible qualification/cost route, and UKTMP can offer uncommitted feed/participation.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if evidence confirms unavailable feed/technology or buyer rejection of the qualification/economic route; PARK if need is sponge-only or viable capital requires splitting/reinventing the package.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: neither upstream qualification nor a global shortage proves a downstream package; retain the exact admitted boundary and test it.

opportunity_name: Integrated aluminium wheels and die castings
investor_capital_decision: Wheel/casting strategic supplier builds the intact integrated aluminium wheels-and-die-castings plant, with Kostanay nominated in the source.
buyer_market: Kazakh/Uzbek vehicle assemblers and rolling-stock builders; product-specific nominations UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S15]: an OEM-group source describes 120,000/year CKD plant capacity and localisation plans; not confirmed component orders.
strongest_realistic_alternative: China-supplied OEM kits and existing approved wheel/casting suppliers; local wheel-capacity lead needs verification. Strongest integrated rival UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: OEM nominations and utilization by wheel/casting specification at competitive delivered cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: aluminium feed and OEM proximity may help; local primary metal does not establish the right alloy, process or price advantage.
scale_view: CALCULATION: approx.120,000 cars/year planning scale x 4 road wheels gives about 0.5m wheels/year for one plant; not actual orders or an integrated-castings forecast [S15].
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: alloy supply, power, casting/heat-treatment capability, qualification and exact plant site.
captured_status: OEM/component capacity exists; unawarded wheels AND castings for the proposed package not established. No full capture concluded.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: qualified component margins plus logistics/localisation value, if both production lines attain viable compatible orders.
cheapest_kill_test: Can the combined plant secure enough unallocated OEM demand at a price beating approved imports?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S15 supports an assembly anchor, not wheel/casting nominations. An indexed Vector Pavlodar capacity lead could not be opened and is not treated as verified market coverage.
key_unknown: Combined order book, actual wheel incumbency and compatibility of wheel/casting capex.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Obtain model-level wheel and casting nominations, verify the Vector/local capacity lead, and compare a supplier minimum-run/cost quote with Chinese delivered parts for the intact package.
pass_condition_if_uwt: Compatible unallocated nominations can sustain both lines and competitive delivered economics; local-feed supply is feasible.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if target orders are demonstrably captured or approved imports undercut sustainable local cost; PARK if viable demand exists only for one line or below the package minimum.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: keep the merged capital package intact; assembly nameplate is a scale cross-check, not proof of investable component demand.

opportunity_name: Automotive wiring-harness plant for vehicle assembly in Kazakhstan
investor_capital_decision: Harness tier-1 supplier builds a Kazakh plant for local Chinese-brand assembly and possible exports; site in original thesis UNKNOWN.
buyer_market: Chinese-brand vehicle assemblers in Kazakhstan; model-specific nomination and harness volumes UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S16]: THN/Astana Motors signed a localisation JV in June 2026, confirming the location decision exists but changing the capture picture.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Signed Kazakhstan Wire Systems programme and China kit suppliers; Uzbekistan is a labour/production candidate, not proven strongest rival.
deciding_location_factor: OEM-approved model nominations, labour productivity and synchronized delivered harness cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local synchronisation/local-content value is plausible; an incumbent approved JV may serve additional Chinese models.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: unallocated model volumes versus supplier minimum run; total vehicle capacity cannot be counted as harness orders.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: drawings/IP, OEM quality nomination, test equipment, trained labour and selected site.
captured_status: FACT [S16]: JV signed; Kia Sportage and Hyundai Tucson launch plans are specified. Future Chinese-brand expansion is a plan, not proof all Chinese orders are captured.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: assembly margin and customer logistics savings if model-specific volume supports labour and engineering costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Which Chinese-brand harness nominations remain genuinely available after the THN JV?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S16 identifies a USD4.6m JV and initial model schedule. Neither this agreement nor future expansion language proves an open competing plant or full market closure.
key_unknown: Residual Chinese-model nominations and delivered labour/engineering economics.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Map the intended Chinese models against THN/JV and kit-supplier nominations; obtain an OEM-approved supplier minimum volume and local-versus-China/Uzbekistan cost comparison.
pass_condition_if_uwt: At least one compatible unallocated OEM programme supports a viable line and a credible local delivered-cost/localisation benefit.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if all target nominations are contractually allocated or viable qualified imports dominate; PARK if residual volumes do not cover a supplier's minimum run.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: signed capture of some models is substantial adverse evidence, but failing the Chinese-brand thesis outright would overstate the source.

opportunity_name: Cattle breeding genetics (breeding stock and semen)
investor_capital_decision: Animal-genetics investor establishes cattle breeding-stock/semen production in Kazakhstan; site/route not established in admitted thesis.
buyer_market: Beef farms/feedlots buying genetics; adoption, price and subsidy-adjusted demand UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S17]: 2026-2030 livestock programme and reproduction pilots; FMD status [S13] is supportive context, not automatic genetics demand.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Asyl Tulik and other domestic breeding programmes plus imported semen/stock; best breed/channel alternative UNKNOWN.
deciding_location_factor: Farmer-paid reproductive outcomes per delivered dose/animal, including distribution and insemination access.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local adaptation and shorter distribution could help; portable imported semen and existing domestic production are credible rivals.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: recurring paid doses/stock by breed and adoption; herd size and unused semen inventory do not equal sales.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: sanitary permissions, donor stock, cryogenic distribution and a certified operating site.
captured_status: FACT [S17]: Asyl Tulik and farm reproduction capability already operate. Incremental need and partner opening UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: repeated genetics sales if improved outcomes justify price beyond import/distribution and service costs.
cheapest_kill_test: Is the bottleneck missing locally produced genetics or access/adoption of existing genetics?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S17 describes existing breeding operations and a mobile insemination pilot. This challenges an assumed empty supply market; it does not prove all farmer demand is met.
key_unknown: Paid incremental demand for production rather than distribution/adoption support.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Compare recent farmer procurement/subsidy data and Asyl Tulik supply/stock with farm demand for one breed; price local production against imported semen with the same insemination service.
pass_condition_if_uwt: A repeat paying customer pool needs locally produced material with a verified outcome/cost or biosecurity advantage at a viable production run.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if buyers prefer adequately available qualified supply below sustainable local cost; PARK if the binding gap is adoption/service delivery rather than the proposed production capital.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: genetics demand is plausible and testable; neither FMD recognition nor an old import figure establishes a production gap.

opportunity_name: Cold-chain warehouses and reefer logistics for meat and produce exports
investor_capital_decision: Cold-chain logistics investor builds refrigerated warehouses/reefer capacity on Kazakh export routes; actual corridor/site UNKNOWN.
buyer_market: Kazakh meat/produce exporters and destination importers paying storage/transport fees; anchor shipments UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S13]: animal-health status improved; an export-volume or cold-capacity increment attributable to it is not established.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Lease existing cold storage and reefer services or direct shipment from processors; Uzbekistan is not automatically a substitute for storing Kazakhstan-origin cargo.
deciding_location_factor: Route-specific year-round paid utilization and total spoilage-adjusted delivered cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: storage near actual Kazakh export flows can reduce spoilage/delay; generic regional growth does not pick a corridor.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: tonnes/month, seasonality and backhaul utilization; aggregate food production cannot size a profitable warehouse.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: destination market access, reliable electricity/refrigeration, border dwell, route time and backup at a selected site.
captured_status: No exclusive route gap or full capture established; incumbent capacity/use needs direct checking.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: contracted storage/reefer fees and reduced loss/delay, if these benefits exceed capital, energy and empty-leg cost.
cheapest_kill_test: Is there a recurring cold-chain gap on an actual permitted export lane rather than just forecast export growth?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S13 establishes FMD status with vaccination, not destination access, paid export flows or warehouse need. No verified corridor-specific cold-capacity dataset was obtained.
key_unknown: A permitted lane with unmet service demand and enough off-season utilization.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Choose one existing exporter lane from the original meat/produce scope; verify destination permissions and monthly flows, compare spare incumbent cold/reefer capacity and route quotes, and calculate break-even utilization.
pass_condition_if_uwt: An identified lane has recurring unserved shipments, legal destination access and anchored utilization whose tariffs cover power, refrigeration and transport costs.
kill_or_park_condition_if_uwt: FAIL if the lane is inaccessible or existing providers meet the required service below viable cost; PARK if seasonality/empty legs leave utilization below quoted break-even.
screening_rationale: JUDGMENT: a useful service mechanism remains testable; no new corridor or integrated food-production business is invented to rescue it.

opportunity_name: Gas turbine service and repair centre
investor_capital_decision: Gas-turbine OEM/qualified service investor builds a Kazakh overhaul centre for power/compressor fleets; site UNKNOWN.
buyer_market: Owners of specific gas turbines and compressors; available overhaul work outside existing agreements UNKNOWN.
why_now: FACT [S20]: southern gas projects are under construction; S19 shows maintenance strategy matters. Harder Russian servicing remains an unverified source assumption.
strongest_realistic_alternative: Existing ZKMK GE-authorised local centre and OEM regional shops; UAE/Turkey only where authorised for the exact model.
deciding_location_factor: OEM/model authorisation and addressable overhaul frequency, with total downtime/transport cost.
kazakhstan_vs_alternative: INFERENCE: local overhaul can save shipment/downtime; an existing Kazakh authorised shop may already offer that advantage.
scale_view: UNKNOWN: paid shop visits/year by model net of LTSA commitments; added MW is not annual overhaul revenue.
physical_constraint_view: UNKNOWN: OEM technology rights, tooling/test benches, engineers and a model-specific shop location.
captured_status: FACT [S18]: local GE service capability established in 2011; S19 notes OEM control of critical maintenance. Residual model/workscope gap UNKNOWN.
economic_return_mechanism: INFERENCE: recurring qualified overhaul/spares margin and downtime savings at sufficient shop utilization.
cheapest_kill_test: Do any target turbine models have an unserved and contractually available overhaul scope?
decisive_evidence: FACT: S18 documents authorised repair facilities; S19 makes OEM restrictions explicit. Neither covers every new model or proves a closed entire fleet.
key_unknown: Residual authorised shop workload after incumbents and OEM long-term service agreements.
next_test_if_uwt: Proposed owner: Batch-03 validator (team to assign); 60-minute desk test: Map models/commissioning dates at two new plants and one compressor operator; inspect OEM/LTSA shop allocation, then compare available visits and turnaround quotes with ZKMK and an authorised overseas shop.
